messages.text:
Thank you for taking part. I'm an AI assistant for this IAM-CC research interview.

We would like to hear your views and experiences to help us understand how ready society is to use and engage with new and emerging technologies. In this interview, we will talk about drones and services that use drones.

There are no right or wrong answers. Your opinions and your own experiences matter. You can skip any question, pause, correct an answer, stop or withdraw at any time.

Please avoid personal names, addresses, contact details and sensitive information. Messages are screened before processing, but screening can miss personal details. Progress is held temporarily in memory; download a copy if you want to keep it. Contact follow-up and cross-day resume are unavailable.

Which point of view would you like to use in this conversation?

A. Citizen
A member of the public answering from their own point of view. For example, a resident, patient, service user, worker, member of a community organisation, or anyone who could be affected by drone services.

B. Organisation or institution
Someone answering on behalf of an organisation involved in planning, providing, regulating, supporting or overseeing drone services. For example, a municipality, regional authority, regulator, policymaker, city planner, transport authority, healthcare organisation, logistics organisation or infrastructure provider.

C. Technology expert or researcher
Someone working directly with drone technology or related technical systems. For example, a drone operator, manufacturer, engineer, researcher, technology developer, take-off and landing infrastructure developer or airspace-service provider.

If more than one applies, please choose the perspective you would prefer to use today.
C. Technology expert or researcher
Thank you. I will ask the following questions from a technical perspective.

Here are some other technical areas that may be relevant. Which two or three are most important for the system you are assessing?
You can choose just one issue if that is what matters to you.
• compatibility with take-off, landing and supporting infrastructure
• energy use, range and emissions
• operating cost and technical efficiency
• ability to serve the intended routes and users reliably
• integration with the wider healthcare and logistics chain
• noise measurement, prediction and mitigation
• visibility of aircraft and infrastructure
• technical features supporting public safety or privacy
• aircraft safety, failure management, cybersecurity and data protection
• wind, turbulence and air movement around take-off and landing areas
• capacity to operate alongside other airspace users and traffic-management systems
• monitoring and performance data
• technical documentation, training and maintenance support

messages.text: I will now show you the scale used to understand your answers. The judgment is provisional and based on self-report.

Provisional result: TRL 6 — Technology demonstrated in a relevant environment.

The technology has been demonstrated under relevant conditions, specifically a hospital-campus route with staff as receiving users, validating integrated navigation, payload temperature control, and dispatch connector performance. While long-duration reliability and extreme weather performance remain untested, the demonstration meets the criteria for a relevant environment as described in the anchor.

Evidence from your answers:
“The demonstration showed route accuracy and payload temperature in a hospital-campus setting, but long-duration reliability and extreme weather performance remain untested. No formal qualification exists for operational use.”
“The demonstration represented the intended service in a controlled hospital-campus environment, but long-duration reliability and extreme weather performance remain untested. No formal qualification exists for operational use.”
“The system was demonstrated in a hospital-campus environment, showing route accuracy and payload temperature control. Long-duration reliability and extreme weather performance remain untested.”

Boundary: Compared with TRL 7 — System prototype demonstrated in the operational environment: The next level,, requires a representative system prototype demonstrated under actual operational conditions. The current evidence only describes a demonstration, not a fully developed prototype, and lacks formal operational qualification.

Now that you have seen the scale and the explanation, how well do you think the provisional TRL 6 result describes the current technical maturity of the system?

A. It describes the system well
B. It mostly describes the system, but something important is missing
C. I think the system should be at a higher level
D. I think the system should be at a lower level
E. I am not sure
E
Which part of the explanation or scale leaves you uncertain? You can also say you have nothing to add.
